title: Retire the Locations extension
summary: The Locations extension is removed. Places are now found only through the Theographic Data extension, which shows each chapter's places in Discover with a small map. On phones, the small map's **Open in map** button used to be hidden; now it opens the place's map in a sheet that slides up from the bottom, and closing it leaves Discover exactly where you were.

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the button above, in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer. Some tests later also need a phone (iPhone Safari or Android Chrome); if you don't have one, a computer browser window made as narrow as it goes (then reloaded) works too. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If it looks like the old version, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac). On a phone, close the tab and open the link again.

setup.title: Start clean and sign in
setup.body: Use a private/incognito window, so nothing is left over from earlier visits. Sign in with your email address (you'll be sent a code, so use an inbox you can check). Installing extensions needs an account.

setup.title: Use a light theme to start
setup.body: The tests assume the app's light theme unless they say otherwise. In these tests, **Discover** is the panel that lists the people, places and events in a chapter. Open it with the **Discover** button (a compass icon) in the reader's toolbar.

sections.title: Locations is gone, Theographic Data takes its place

tests.title: Locations is no longer offered as an extension
steps: Open **Settings**, then **Extensions**.
Look through both the **Installed** and **Available** lists.
expected: There is no extension called **Locations** in either list.
**Theographic Data** is listed.

tests.title: Theographic Data installs normally
steps: In **Extensions**, install **Theographic Data** from **Available** (if it's already under **Installed**, leave it).
Close Settings and open **Genesis 10**.
expected: Theographic Data moves to **Installed** without an error message.
Genesis 10 loads and reads normally.

tests.title: A selected verse has no Locations button
tests.why: Locations used to add a **Locations** button to the verse toolbar for verses that name a place.
steps: On a computer at full width, open **John 2** and click verse **John 2:1** (it mentions Cana).
Look at the buttons in the verse toolbar, including any **More** menu.
expected: There is no **Locations** button and no **Show Cana on map** option.
The usual buttons (Highlight, Save, Note, Copy, and so on) are all there and work.

sections.title: Place maps on a computer
sections.intro: These tests use a full-width browser window on a computer.

tests.title: A place card in Discover shows a small map with an Open in map button
steps: Open **Genesis 10** and open **Discover**.
Open the **Places** section (or tap the **Places** chip) and click a place card, for example **Babel** or **Nineveh**, so it expands.
expected: The expanded card shows a small map of the place.
In the small map's top-right corner is a button; hovering over it shows **Open in map**.

tests.title: Open in map opens a floating window on a computer
tests.before: The place card from the previous test is still expanded.
steps: Click the **Open in map** button in the small map's corner.
Look at the card in Discover while the window is open.
Close the floating window with its close button.
expected: The place's map opens in a floating window titled with the place's name.
While the window is open, the card no longer shows its own small map.
After closing the window, the card's small map comes back.

sections.title: Place maps on a phone
sections.intro: Before this change, phones didn't show the **Open in map** button at all.

setup.title: Switch to a phone
setup.body: Open the preview link on a phone, signed in with the same account (Theographic Data stays installed). Or make a computer browser window as narrow as it goes (about 480 pixels or less) and reload.

tests.title: Open in map opens a sheet from the bottom, and the card keeps its space
tests.why: New in this PR: on a phone the map opens in a sheet over Discover instead of a full-screen panel, which would close Discover.
steps: Open **Genesis 10** and open **Discover**.
Open **Places**, then scroll Discover partway down so the list isn't at the very top. Tap a place card to expand it.
Tap the **Open in map** button in the corner of its small map.
expected: A sheet slides up from the bottom with the place's name at the top and its map filling most of the sheet.
Behind the sheet, Discover is still showing (not replaced by a full-screen map).
The list behind the sheet doesn't jump or shrink: the card keeps an empty box where its small map was.

tests.title: Closing the sheet puts you back where you were
tests.before: The map sheet from the previous test is open.
steps: Remember which card is near the top of the screen behind the sheet.
Close the sheet with its **X**.
Open the same map again, then this time close the sheet by tapping outside it (on the dimmed area above it).
expected: Both ways, the sheet closes and Discover is at the same scroll position as before.
The place card is still expanded and its small map is back.

tests.title: The map in the sheet can be moved and zoomed
steps: Open a place's map in its sheet again.
Drag the map with one finger and pinch to zoom in and out.
expected: The map moves and zooms. The sheet itself doesn't close or slide while you do this.
The map stays inside the sheet with no blank or cut-off area.

tests.title: A place in the verse sheet opens its map the same way
tests.why: On phones, the panel that slides up when you tap a verse also lists that verse's places.
steps: Close Discover and go back to the text of **Genesis 10**. Tap verse **Genesis 10:10** (it mentions Babel and other places).
Swipe the verse sheet open and scroll down inside it to the **Places** section. Expand a place card.
Scroll the verse sheet up and down so the small map passes under the buttons at the top of the sheet.
Tap **Open in map**, then close the map's sheet by tapping outside it.
expected: While scrolling, the small map and its button slide underneath the sheet's buttons, never on top of them.
The map opens in its own sheet from the bottom.
Closing it returns you to the verse sheet with **Genesis 10:10** still selected.

tests.title: The map sheet looks right in dark mode
steps: Switch the app to its dark theme in **Settings**.
Open Discover on **Genesis 10**, expand a place card, and tap **Open in map**.
expected: The sheet's title and **X** are readable against the dark background.
Nothing appears as a white box with no content, and nothing runs off the edge of the screen.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Places show in other translations
tests.why: Locations only worked in English; Theographic is meant to work in every translation.
steps: Switch to a non-English translation (for example Spanish) and open **Genesis 10**.
Open **Discover** and the **Places** section.
expected: The **Places** section lists places for the chapter, much like in English, and their small maps load.

tests.title: A phone rotated sideways with the map open (known gap)
tests.why: The PR says this case is not fixed yet: after rotating with the sheet open, Discover may end up scrolled slightly off. Record what you see so it can be judged; a small jump here is expected, a broken page is not.
steps: On a phone, open a place's map sheet from Discover.
Rotate the phone sideways, then back upright, then close the sheet.
expected: The page doesn't break, the sheet closes normally, and the place card shows its small map again.
Discover may be scrolled a little away from where you were (this is the known gap).

notCovered: Removing the Locations code, its translation file and its tests, and the unused location icon. There's nothing to see for these beyond Locations being absent.
The browser console message ("not available, skipping") shown to readers who had Locations installed before. It's only visible in developer tools.
